links.outcome: Alignment with scientific consensus of retrieval-augmented LLM versus baseline LLM
links.effect: Consensus improved from 46.5% to 84.0% (difference 37.5%; 95% CI 29.0%-46.0%; P<.001); not different from GPT-4 (79.2%).
links.quote: Our LLM surpassed the baseline model in aligning with scientific consensus, improving consensus from 46.5% to 84.0% (difference = 37.5%; 95% CI, 29.0%-46.0%; P < .001) and not different from GPT-4 with a value of 79.2% (difference = 4.8%; 95% CI, −0.3% to 10.0%; P = .06).

links.outcome: Answers with no inappropriate or erroneous content, retrieval-augmented versus baseline
links.effect: 74.8% no inappropriate/erroneous content vs 32.0% for baseline (difference 42.8%; 95% CI 40.0%-44.8%; P<.001); GPT-4 74.2%.
links.quote: In safety assessments, our LLM generated 74.8% answers with no inappropriate or erroneous content, compared with 32.0% (difference = 42.8%; 95% CI, 40.0%-44.8%; P < .001) for the baseline model and 74.2% (difference = 0.6%; 95% CI, −1.5% to 2.7%; P = .50) for GPT-4, respectively.

links.outcome: Human ranking score of candidate LLMs compared on the same 300 questions
links.effect: Ten LLMs benchmarked; ChatZOC scored 0.60 vs baseline 0.48 (difference 0.12; P=.02) and GPT-4 0.61 (P=.89).
links.quote: Evaluation using 300 questions sampled from the COD showed that the human ranking score of our ophthalmic LLM had achieved a score of 0.60, different from the baseline model of 0.48 (difference = 0.12; 95% CI, 0.02-0.22; P = .02) and not different from GPT-4 with a score of 0.61 (difference = 0.01; 95% CI, −0.11 to 0.13; P = .89), as shown in Table 2 .
